scope: A separate literature-reviewed temporal foreground derived from premise's coastal olivine inventory. Original workbook unchanged. This review does not certify coastal field performance.
functional_unit: One deployment unit = 1.25 kg olivine-rich rock. Source-based eventual gross uptake potential is 1 kg CO2 before an additional realization sensitivity. It is not a guaranteed kilogram of net removal. Slides scale deployment by 1000.

findings.title: Reference-product description
findings.evidence: The old description calls this a kilogram of rock although the reference exchange is a kilogram of captured CO2 and uses 1.25 kg rock.
findings.action: Use a deployment service in units, explicitly linked to fixed rock mass and eventual potential.

findings.title: Comminution electricity voltage
findings.evidence: Table S1 specifies European medium-voltage electricity. The workbook names a low-voltage market. The 10 µm total is 92.3+0.22+0.33+0.22 = 93.07 kWh/tCO2.
findings.action: Change the grinding supplier and reference product to medium voltage; retain 0.09307 kWh per deployment unit.
findings.status: Source-supported mapping correction; linking to a selected database remains to be checked.

findings.title: Nickel compartment and amount
findings.evidence: The workbook splits Ni between ocean and long-term groundwater using a first-year dissolution fraction. A delayed release to seawater does not establish a groundwater emission. Exact source mass arithmetic gives 1.25 × 0.00263 = 0.0032875 kg Ni/unit, versus rounded 0.00329.
findings.action: Keep one ocean Ni exchange; attach its dated release as a conservative congruent-dissolution upper bound. Do not infer a measured mobile fraction.
findings.status: Compartment corrected; temporal mobility remains an explicit upper-bound scenario.

findings.title: Atmospheric uptake timing
findings.evidence: The source paper models delayed dissolution. The later marine-weathering review distinguishes mineral reaction, alkalinity transfer and atmospheric equilibration.
findings.action: Distribute resource CO2 uptake using a shrinking-core dissolution curve convolved with an air–sea delay kernel. Never add a second negative credit for alkalinity production.
findings.status: Mechanistically motivated temporal scenario; 10/30-year durations and 1/5-year lag choices are not site-calibrated estimates.

findings.title: Water and transport arithmetic
findings.evidence: The workbook totals 0.00049612 m3 water per unit, consistent with the SI's cooling, dust suppression and drilling water combined. Coastal haulage is 1.25 kg × 50 km /1000 = 0.0625 tkm per unit.
findings.action: Retain these quantities and their existing aggregation; do not add the source rows a second time.

findings.title: ecoinvent 3.12 supplier identities
findings.evidence: The original EURO3/5/6 truck names do not match the renamed ecoinvent 3.12 datasets.
findings.action: Use the exact same size, diesel fuel and EURO class with current name/product/location identities; preserve quantities.
findings.status: Exact TRAILS import passed with no unlinked exchanges.

findings.title: Repeated electricity supplier coordinate
findings.evidence: Correcting grinding to medium voltage makes it share an identity with pumping electricity.
findings.action: Aggregate their amounts and retain both comments; distinct temporal profiles remain separate.
findings.status: Calculated input retains 0.093120605 kWh per deployment unit.

temporal_scenario: The active lecture case now deploys the same total rock in twenty equal annual batches, 2030–2049, with year-specific background suppliers and FaIR recalculated. The original single-batch foreground and results are retained for provenance. Deployment-year foreground inputs are retained. Three variants: static reference, 10-year shrinking-core dissolution with a 1-year exponential air–sea lag and full reference realization, and a slower 30-year/5-year/80% realization sensitivity. These are fixed-deployment scenarios; they are not paired particle-size/energy variants. Ni is a separate conservative upper bound and is not reduced with atmospheric realization.
limitations: The 2023 paper's 0.8 kg CO2/kg rock potential already accounts conservatively for composition/buffering; the additional realization sensitivity must not be interpreted as a second universal carbonate correction.
The hydraulic manure-spreader substitution is retained as a spreading proxy. Its loading overlap and suitability are unresolved; do not present it as a verified lime-spreading inventory.
The extra 0.0125 tkm quarry-to-crusher proxy is retained. The source SI lists an ELCD mining-truck proxy in kg rather than a verified equivalent transport distance.
Source SI land-restoration rows are absent from the inherited workbook. No restoration or associated carbon credit has been invented without a quarry life and site plan.
Site hydrodynamics, sediment reactions, secondary minerals, alkalinity additionality, biological responses and site-specific air–sea exchange require further evidence.
The Ni mass is a total mobilization upper bound, not observed dissolved concentration or proof of ecological safety. Other metal releases and turbidity remain unquantified.
The calculated snapshots use the corrected linked foreground. Dated LCI uses fixed depth one with complete residual background solves; full upstream temporal-routing convergence has not been tested.

The live uptake controls vary only foreground timing and realization, holding the calculated upstream inventory fixed. They do not rerun FaIR or LCA, or implement matched particle-size/energy variants.

timing_evidence.scope: The displayed 10-year dissolution / 1-year air–sea timescale is a fast illustrative reference, not a commonly agreed field window. The shaded cumulative GWP band spans selected timing scenarios and has no probability interpretation.
findings: Foteinis et al. (2023) used a ten-year shrinking-core dissolution assumption for the 10-micrometre base case. This does not establish a universal Northern European field rate.
Geerts et al. (2025) discuss full olivine-sand dissolution over 10–500 years under field conditions, depending on initial grain size. Mineral reaction and atmospheric uptake are different processes.

He & Tyka (2023) report substantial coastal air–sea equilibration after 3–4 years at many modelled sites and 8–10 years at some; deep-ocean return can extend for centuries. These are not fitted values for our exponential delay parameter.
Our one-year lag is an exponential-kernel timescale, not a hard one-year delay or a guarantee of complete uptake in that year.

The band varies CO2 uptake timing over 10/1, 30/5 and 100/5-year scenarios for the same twenty annual batches, holding supplier inventory, total rock and eventual reference uptake potential fixed. It is not a matched particle-size/energy study, site calibration, or full uncertainty interval.
